description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Increased access to finance for MSMEs: Financial inclusion remains a challenge in Morocco. MSMEs in Morocco face a financing gap of US$ 20.4billion. Access to finance challenges are even more acute for women-owned businesses. IFCs financing will help Arrawaj expand its MSME portfolio, with a particular focus on the very small enterprises (VSEs). The Project is also expected to make a significant contribution towards expanding reach to women-owned MSMEs.
Competitiveness: Beyond the project outcomes, the Project is expected to strengthen the competitiveness of Moroccos microfinance sector, contributing to improved market discipline, broadening the range of financial products available, and enhancing sector efficiency.

The proposed investment consists of a senior loan to Fondation Arrawaj de la Finance Inclusive (Arrawaj or the Borrower), Moroccos third-largest microcredit association, to support its lending program to micro and small enterprises, including women owned businesses. The financing will be provided in U.S. dollars (USD), euros (EUR), or in Moroccan dirham (MAD) equivalent, with a maturity of up to five years. The project is processed under the MSME Finance Platform (BOP envelope).
